title: Eukaryotic Cell Organelles
topicTitle: Detail structure of eukaryotic cells: cell wall, cell membrane, mitochondria, plastids, endoplasmic reticulum, golgi bodies, lysosomes, ribosomes, nucleus, chromosomes, cilia, flagella and cell inclusions

notes: DETAILED ORGANELLE ANALYSIS (plant + animal cell).

Plasma membrane: phospholipid bilayer (heads out, tails in) + integral proteins (channels, pumps, receptors) + peripheral proteins + cholesterol + glycocalyx (cell recognition). Fluid-mosaic model (Singer & Nicolson, 1972).

Mitochondrion: double membrane; outer smooth, inner folded into cristae; matrix with Krebs enzymes; own DNA + 70S ribosomes (endosymbiosis); aerobic respiration: glycolysis (cytoplasm) → Krebs (matrix) → ETS (cristae) → ~34 ATP.

Chloroplast: double membrane; thylakoids stacked into grana; stroma with Calvin-cycle enzymes; chlorophyll a + b; own DNA + 70S ribosomes; light reactions (grana → ATP, NADPH, O2) + Calvin cycle (stroma → glucose).

Nucleus: nuclear envelope (4 nm, two membranes, pores); nucleoplasm; chromatin (DNA + histone proteins); nucleolus (rRNA + ribosome assembly).
Rough ER (RER): ribosomes on outer surface → protein synthesis (secretory + membrane proteins); continuous with nuclear envelope.
Smooth ER (SER): lipid synthesis, carbohydrate metabolism, detoxification (liver), Ca2+ storage (muscle — sarcoplasmic reticulum).
Golgi apparatus: cisternae + vesicles; modifies (glycosylation), packages, sorts, and secretes proteins; forms lysosomes + cell plate (plants).
Lysosomes: 8–12 nm vesicle, hydrolytic enzymes (acidic pH); digest food particles, worn organelles (autophagy); "suicide bags" when damaged.

**Organelle specialisations — who has what (highly classified)**

| Organelle | Plant cell | Animal cell | Why the difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cell wall | Present (cellulose) | Absent | Turgor pressure needs a rigid box |
| Plastids | Present | Absent | Plants make their own food |
| Large central vacuole | Present (up to 90% volume) | Small vesicles only | Water storage + turgor |
| Centrioles | Absent (higher plants) | Present | Spindle forms differently in plants |
| Lysosomes | Few (vacuole takes the role) | Many | Animals ingest whole particles |
| Mitochondria + ER + Golgi | Present | Present | Core eukaryote machinery shared |
Vacuole: plant — large central (turgor, storage); animal — small (excretion, osmoregulation, contractile in protozoa).
Cytoskeleton: microfilaments (actin), intermediate filaments, microtubules (tubulin); shape, movement, intracellular transport, division (spindle).
Centrioles (animal): microtubule rings; form the spindle during mitosis; absent in most plants.
Cell inclusions: storage granules (starch, fat, glycogen), pigments (leuco-, chro-, heterochromoplasts), crystalloids.
Cell wall (plant): cellulose microfibrils (primary wall) + pectin; secondary wall with lignin; fully permeable; provides rigidity + protection.

**Deep dive — the plasma membrane as a gatekeeper.** The phospholipid bilayer is hydrophobic in its core, so only small non-polar molecules cross freely. Everything else needs help: channels and carriers for ions and sugars (facilitated diffusion), and ATP-driven pumps against gradients (active transport — the sodium-potassium pump is the classic). Fluid-mosaic is the name because proteins drift in a fluid lipid sea, and the mosaic of glycoproteins is how cells recognise each other.
confusion: RER makes PROTEIN; SER makes LIPID. A cell secreting lots of protein has abundant RER + Golgi (e.g., pancreatic acinar cell).
The Golgi does NOT synthesise proteins; it MODIFIES, SORTS, and PACKAGES what the RER made.
Mitochondria and chloroplasts have their OWN DNA + 70S ribosomes — the key endosymbiosis evidence.
Lysosomes are animal-cell organelles; plants use the large vacuole for hydrolytic digestion.
Cilia and flagella share the 9+2 axonemal microtubule structure; centrioles (9+0) are related but lack the central pair.
The nucleus is NOT the only place with DNA: mitochondria + chloroplasts carry their own genomes.

Mitochondria and chloroplasts reproduce by binary fission, like bacteria.
The nuclear envelope is continuous with the outer membrane of the RER.
A typical human cell has ~500 mitochondria, varying by energy demand.
examples: Secretory protein pathway: ribosome (free) → RER → Golgi → transport vesicle → plasma membrane (exocytosis).
Mitochondrial respiration: glucose → pyruvate (cytoplasm) → Krebs (matrix) → ETS (cristae) → ATP.
Chloroplast photosynthesis: light reactions in grana → ATP + NADPH; Calvin cycle in stroma → glucose.
Lysosome autophagy: damaged mitochondrion → autophagosome → lysosomal digestion → recycled.

enrichedContent.summary: A detailed examination of the eukaryotic cell shows how each membrane-bound organelle specialises a metabolic function. The fluid-mosaic plasma membrane controls transport; mitochondria and chloroplasts convert energy (and carry their own DNA, evidence of endosymbiosis); RER makes protein while SER makes lipid; the Golgi modifies and packages; lysosomes digest; the nucleus and nucleolus control heredity; and the cytoskeleton (microfilaments, microtubules) maintains shape and drives division. The protein-secretion pathway (ribosome → RER → Golgi → vesicle → membrane) and the plant/animal cell contrast are core NEB written-answer topics.
specialNotes: NEB written answers expect a labelled organelle diagram + a one-line function per organelle.
The endosymbiotic theory (4 evidence lines: own DNA, 70S ribosomes, double membrane, binary fission) is a favourite 4-mark question.
Trace the secreted-protein pathway step by step.
Contrast plant vs animal cell (wall, chloroplast, large vacuole vs centrioles, lysosomes).
RER/SER distinction is a very common short-answer.
importantStatements: The plasma membrane is the selectively permeable boundary of every cell.
Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration; chloroplasts of photosynthesis.
The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids.
Cilia, flagella, and centrioles are built from microtubules.

exercises.question: Trace the pathway of a protein made by a ribosome that is to be secreted from the cell.
steps: Ribosome on RER synthesises the protein
Protein enters the RER lumen and is folded
Transport vesicle carries it to the Golgi
Secretory vesicle moves to the plasma membrane
exercises.answer: Ribosome (RER) → RER → Golgi → secretory vesicle → plasma membrane → exocytosis

subtopics.name: Cell membrane detail
points: Phospholipid bilayer ~7-8 nm thick; hydrophilic heads outward, hydrophobic tails inward
Integral proteins span the bilayer; peripheral proteins sit on one face
Glycoproteins and glycolipids on the outer surface form the glycocalyx used in recognition

subtopics.name: Cell wall detail
points: Cellulose microfibrils in a hemicellulose and pectin matrix
Primary wall is thin and extensible; secondary wall is thick and lignified
Plasmodesmata are channels through walls connecting adjacent plant cells

subtopics.name: Mitochondria and plastids
points: Mitochondrion: outer membrane, inner membrane with cristae, intermembrane space, matrix
Chloroplast: outer and inner membrane, stroma, thylakoid membranes stacked into grana
Both contain circular DNA and 70S ribosomes — evidence of endosymbiotic origin

subtopics.name: Endomembrane organelles
points: Rough ER studded with ribosomes for protein synthesis; smooth ER for lipid synthesis and detoxification
Golgi: cis and trans faces, glycosylation and sorting
Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes at acidic pH; peroxisomes handle hydrogen peroxide

subtopics.name: Nucleus and chromosomes
points: Nuclear envelope is double with pores; nucleolus makes rRNA
Chromatin is nucleosomes (DNA wound on histone octamers)
Chromosome number is species-specific and constant

subtopics.name: Cilia and flagella
points: 9+2 microtubule arrangement: nine doublets around a central pair
Dynein motors generate sliding that produces bending
Cilia are short and numerous; flagella are long and few

subtopics.name: Compartment logic
points: Each organelle maintains a distinct internal pH and enzyme set
Lysosomal enzymes work at ~pH 5, protecting the cytosol at pH ~7.2
Membrane identity is set by lipid composition and surface protein markers

subtopics.name: Cell inclusions
points: Non-living accumulations: starch grains, oil droplets, pigment granules, crystals
Glycogen granules in liver and muscle
Inclusions are storage or waste, not organelles
